message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data built into this chat, so I can’t tell you the exact Air Quality Index (AQI) for Los Angeles at this moment. However, you can quickly check the current conditions using one of the following reliable sources:

| Source | How to Use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit <https://www.airnow.gov/> and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. It shows the AQI, pollutant breakdown, and health recommendations. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to <https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/>. It provides a live AQI gauge, historical trends, and forecast. |
| **Weather Apps** | Most weather apps (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, or the built‑in weather app on iOS/Android) display AQI for major cities. |
| **Local News** | Many local news stations (e.g., ABC7, KTLA) report on air quality during severe pollution events. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, you can also use a voice assistant (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and say something like “What’s the air quality in Los Angeles?” They’ll pull the latest data from their respective APIs.

Let me know if you’d like a deeper dive into what the AQI numbers mean or how to interpret the pollutant breakdown!
